title: The Island of Stability
description: Past the end of the periodic table, magic numbers promise superheavy nuclei that last. Unlocks the Nuclide Forge.

puzzle.goal: Treat a nucleus of Z protons and A nucleons as a charged liquid drop. Its binding energy gains a fixed amount per nucleon from the bulk, loses some from the surface (∝ A^(2/3)), from the mutual repulsion of the protons (∝ Z(Z−1)/A^(1/3)) and from any imbalance between neutrons and protons (∝ (A − 2Z)²/A), plus a small pairing correction. Write the binding energy.
puzzle.name: Semi-empirical mass formula (Bethe–Weizsäcker liquid drop)
puzzle.ask: Fission sets in when the Coulomb term outgrows twice the surface term; the fissility is x = (aC Z²/A^(1/3)) / (2 aS A^(2/3)). Find x for flerovium-298 (Z = 114, A = 298) with aS = @{aS} MeV and aC = @{aC} MeV.

vars.a: coefficient (a_V volume, a_S surface, a_C Coulomb, a_A asymmetry)

puzzle.method: Volume energy ∝ A; the surface ∝ R² ∝ A^(2/3); Coulomb energy of a uniformly charged sphere ∝ Z(Z−1)/R; the Pauli principle penalises N ≠ Z quadratically.
